questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 63 degrees. What is the other co-interior angle?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to 180 degrees. The other angle = 180 - 63 = 117 degrees.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The alternate angles are (3x + 20) degrees and (5x - 16) degrees. What is the size of each angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal: 3x + 20 = 5x - 16. So 36 = 2x, giving x = 18. Each angle = 3(18) + 20 = 74 degrees.

questions.stem: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. An angle at the first intersection is 52 degrees (above the line, right of the transversal). What is the corresponding angle at the second intersection?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles between parallel lines are equal. The corresponding angle is 52 degrees.

questions.stem: Lines AB and CD are parallel. A transversal creates angle ABE = 55 degrees at B. Angle BEF = 90 degrees where E is between the parallel lines and EF meets CD at F. What is angle EFC?
questions.explanation: Angle ABE = 55 degrees, so the angle between the transversal BE and AB on the other side = 180 - 55 = 125 degrees. In triangle BEF, angle BEF = 90 degrees. Angle EBF = 55 degrees (alternate to ABE is not directly applicable here). Using co-interior angles: angle ABE + angle BEF + the remaining angles show that angle EFD (alternate to ABE) = 55 degrees. So angle EFC = 180 - 55 = 145 degrees (angles on a straight line at F). Alternatively: the co-interior angles ABE and EFD sum to 180, so EFD = 125 degrees... Let me reconsider. If we trace: ABE = 55 degrees. The line BEF acts as a transversal. Angle ABF (at B, between AB and BF) = 55 degrees. Corresponding angle at F between CD and FB = 55 degrees (angle DFB = 55 degrees). Therefore angle EFC = 180 - 55 = 145 degrees if E and C are on the same side. The answer is 145 degrees.

questions.stem: A transversal crosses two lines. The co-interior angles are 75 degrees and 105 degrees. Are the lines parallel?

options.text: Yes, because co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees
No, because co-interior angles should be equal
No, because the angles do not sum to 360 degrees
Yes, because the angles are supplementary to each other

questions.explanation: By the converse of the co-interior angles rule, if co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees (75 + 105 = 180), then the lines are parallel.
